title: Genrupt: From AI Generation to Paid Seller Workflows
description: Helped Genrupt turn AI generation into paid Amazon seller workflows with billing, recoverable jobs, and controlled agent access.
seoTitle: Genrupt Project | From AI MVP to Paid Operations
seoDescription: How Genrupt turned AI generation into paid Amazon seller workflows with billing, recoverable jobs, and controlled agent access.
role: Billing, credit accounting, background jobs, seller workflows, and agent access
deliveryHighlights: Organization accounts, subscriptions, billing, and credit-ledger accounting for paid seller teams
Retryable background jobs for long-running image, video, storyboard, and Amazon seller workflows
Permissioned MCP tools for approved external-agent workflows
Market analysis, Amazon review scraping, listing-builder, and A+ content workflows
constraints: The product had to support paying customers while the platform surface kept expanding.
Long-running generation jobs needed to retry safely without drifting credits or billing state.
Agent-facing workflows had to stay narrow, permissioned, and recoverable instead of exposing the whole internal app surface.
problem: Genrupt could generate AI images and video, but seller teams could not yet subscribe, share organization accounts, or rely on credits staying correct when a long-running job retried.
Each new Amazon seller workflow increased the risk of slower releases and billing mistakes unless jobs, credits, and status stayed connected.
Seller workflows also needed to run from internal chat and external AI agents without exposing app routes, IDs, or background job mechanics.
solution: Worked alongside Genrupt's founder to turn product direction into shipped Amazon seller workflows for market research, review intelligence, listing generation, and A+ content.
Shipped organization accounts, subscriptions, credit accounting, automatic payment updates, and cost controls for paid seller teams.
Added status, retry, and recovery paths for long-running image, video, storyboard, and seller jobs without drifting credits or billing state.
Built a permissioned MCP surface so paid users could run approved seller workflows from external AI agents without exposing the product's internal routes or job mechanics.
result: Seller teams could subscribe, share organization accounts, buy credits, and receive automatic payment updates.
This work helped Genrupt support its first 200 paying customers.
External AI agents could run approved seller workflows without access to the internal app architecture.
Long-running generation and seller jobs could recover from failures without routine manual babysitting.
